root_cause.text: The vulnerability arises because the host-side driver only processes DBC deactivation transactions from the device in the context of a user ioctl; if the user process exits before that transaction is received and handled, the host never releases the DBC resources, leading to a permanent resource leak and a potential hang when another user tries to activate the same DBC.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states, “if the user goes away before receiving and handling the deactivation, the host will be out-of-sync with the DBCs available for use, and the DBC resources will not be freed unless the device is removed.” The patch adds handling for QAIC_TRANS_DEACTIVATE_FROM_DEV in `resp_worker()` when the response has no matching waiting request (i.e., the user is gone), and modifies `decode_deactivate()` to skip reassignment when `usr` is NULL.
